observations.content: Bootstrapped Doxa's standard landing-gate infrastructure into doxa-mcp-schema (2026-08-11): KG Guard + Claude Code Review CI workflows, kg-save/review/test PreToolUse hooks, attest-review.sh, knowledge-graph-merkle.js + ontology-guard.js + kg-index.js, .claude/settings.json hook wiring. Ported from openclaw's working reference implementation per doxa-cns CLAUDE.md PR-visibility / bank-the-gold / kg-save-on-every-merge doctrine. test-gate.sh code_re scoped to server/src + server/scripts + clients/typescript/src (schemas/examples/docs excluded — this repo is mostly schema+docs). NOTE: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret not yet configured on GitHub for this repo — review workflow is inert until Garth adds it.
Propagated the 2026-08-11 atomic-write and --type-guard fixes from doxa-cns's canonical knowledge-graph-merkle.js.

New standing gate (2026-08-13, Garth: 'standing doctrine and practice across all repos'): merge-resolve CLI command unions both sides of a .knowledge-graph-merkle.json conflict by observation hash instead of picking one (the observations array is an append log; checkout --ours/--theirs always drops data). check-kg-merge-integrity.js is the mechanical detector wired into kg-save-gate.sh: for any merge commit in the landing range, if the result is missing an observation hash present in a parent, the landing is blocked and the specific dropped entity is named. Ported from doxa-cns's canonical version, built and verified against the real incident that motivated it (PR #343's KgAddTrailingTypeFlagFix entity, silently dropped by checkout --theirs).

Code-review hardening (2026-08-13, propagated from doxa-cns's fixed feat/kg-merge-resolve): (1) PLACEMENT — kg-save-gate.sh's merge-integrity check now runs immediately after cwd/worktree validation, before the repo_common and base/empty-range early-exits, so a landing that previously exited 0 before reaching a later-placed check can no longer skip it. (2) FAIL-OPEN — check-kg-merge-integrity.js wraps main() in a top-level try/catch that exits 0 on any internal error, so a bug in the detector itself can never masquerade as a confirmed violation and block a legitimate landing. (3) MALFORMED-HASH COLLAPSE — observationsAt() and mergeResolve()'s union loop both now require typeof obs.hash === 'string' && obs.hash.length > 0, skipping anything else instead of silently collapsing multiple malformed observations onto one Map key. (4) NON-DETERMINISM — mergeResolve()'s sort adds a secondary hash tie-break so observations sharing an exact timestamp no longer break ties by argument-dependent insertion order. (5) mergeResolve() guards JSON.parse with try/catch for friendly errors instead of raw stack traces, and the CLI help text no longer overclaims that merge-resolve is needed for graph.json conflicts (graph.json is a pure projection, always correctly regenerated by reconcile()). Verified via 2 new test files (merge-resolve.test.js, kg-save-gate-merge-integrity.test.js) plus the existing suite, 16/16 passing.

Fixed a review finding on the hardening commit (1c0d11c): mergeResolve()'s 'unique to ours/theirs' console summary computed onlyInOurs/onlyInTheirs as merged.length minus RAW (unfiltered) oursCount/theirsCount, so malformed entries — excluded from merged but still counted in the raw lengths — could push the subtraction negative and silently suppress a genuinely-unique observation's report (no data loss, cosmetic only, verified by a synchronous independent code-review agent that ran the pre/post-fix tests to confirm). Fixed by counting via set membership over each side's valid hashes instead of length subtraction. Added a regression test.

The kg-guard job now carries an explicit 'name: KG Guard'. Without it the job reports its check-run under the bare job id 'check' — which is what a branch ruleset's required-status-check has to match on, so requiring it was both ambiguous (any other workflow with a job id 'check' collides) and unreadable in the PR checks list. Prerequisite for the 2026-08-15 fleet-wide enforcement pass: KG Guard ran on PRs in every repo but was a REQUIRED check in none of them, so the banking doctrine rested entirely on the merger choosing to wait for green — the local .claude/hooks/kg-save-gate.sh only binds Claude sessions in that checkout, and web-UI merges bypass everything.

npm pack in clients/typescript leaves thedoxaway-mcp-client-<version>.tgz in the tree. Untracked and unbanked until the 2026-09-02 fleet sweep; now gitignored so a build artifact can never be committed by accident.

Brand presence audit 2026-09-28: the official MCP registry listing io.github.TheDoxaWay/doxa-mcp (versions 1.0.0-1.0.3) had no icons, so registry clients showed a blank tile. server.json 1.0.4 adds icons from doxa.app (favicon.svg any-size + favicon-512x512.png), both the Doxa app icon (white mountains mark on #FF4500, website canon). Publish with mcp-publisher login github -token (gh token of an org member) then mcp-publisher publish; the previous registry JWT in ~/.config/mcp-publisher/token.json had expired. Glama (glama.ai/mcp/servers/The-Doxa-Way/doxa-mcp-schema) already shows the app icon; its meta line still quotes an older README (the Doxa Way journey map, BYOL for unlimited) and refreshes from the repo.

Correction (review round): Glama's meta line quotes old README text (BYOL for unlimited, free per-individual quota, Scripture, summoned.); the Doxa Way journey map is current README copy. Whether Glama refreshes from the repo is unverified. Icon order: the PNG is icons[0] because clients MUST support PNG but only SHOULD support SVG.

2026-10-11 (Garth: the org owns it, not the account): Doxa MCP is listed in the official MCP registry as io.github.The-Doxa-Way/doxa-mcp, 1.0.4 published + verified active with both doxa.app icons. Publish: garthhiltonwatson org membership made PUBLIC, then mcp-publisher login github --token "$(gh auth token)" (JWT lasts ~5 min) and publish — no browser. Remote URL is https://doxa.app/mcp/v1?src=registry because the registry allows one server per remote URL and the bare URL is owned by the legacy io.github.TheDoxaWay/doxa-mcp (1.0.0-1.0.3), which is the USER namespace of the separate GitHub user TheDoxaWay; only that user can deprecate it. Corrects BrandPresenceAudit0928 ('gh token of an org member' could never publish a user namespace).

2026-10-24: review-gate.sh narrows attestation candidates to the merged PR's real head SHA (wrapper merge_gate_head_sha, else gh pr view on MCP pullNumber or the gh-pr-merge argument); unresolved = fail-open to local tips. Fixes gate-health NO_PR_HEAD_RESOLUTION (any attested local branch admitted any PR by number). Shared snippet with doxa-cns #1844; test scripts/review-gate-head.test.mjs.

2026-10-26: the registry listing, README badge and npm client description no longer say 'faith.tools 5/5', which read as a grade from faith.tools. They now say the faith.tools rubric was SELF-RUN by Doxa against the live endpoint (5/5 critical-fail); faith.tools has not graded Doxa. server.json 1.0.5 (description 100 chars, the registry cap). Rule: never describe a self-run check as an independent evaluation. Source: growth radar 2026-10-26 item 2. Follow-on: doxa.app blog posts (add-bible-mcp-claude-desktop-60-seconds, choosing-a-christian-mcp, christian-ai-what-to-look-for-2026) still say 'independently evaluated'.

Publish state at merge (2026-10-26): registry 1.0.5 is published by mcp-publisher after this PR merges. npm @thedoxaway/mcp-client 0.2.5 carries the fixed description but is NOT published yet: this Mac has no npm login (E401); live npm 0.2.4 still says 'independent faith.tools rubric' until the next npm publish.

2026-10-27: publishing 1.0.5 left 1.0.4 'active' in registry search, still showing 'faith.tools 5/5'. Deprecated 1.0.4 (mcp-publisher status --status deprecated, verified via /v0/servers?search=doxa: only 1.0.5 active). PUBLISHING.md 'Updates later' now makes deprecating the replaced version part of every publish.
